title: Kano air disaster
summary: A Boeing 707 crashed at Kano International Airport while attempting to land in high winds. The aircraft landed nose wheel first and the nose wheel collapsed after hitting a depression in the runway. The right main landing gear subsequently collapsed, the aircraft turned 180 degrees, left the runway and burst into flames. All 176 fatalities were a result of the fire.
probable_cause: The Nigerian government concluded pilot error caused the crash by flying the aircraft in a reckless manner in high wind conditions. The nose wheel collapsed after hitting a runway depression.

factors.evidence: Kano International Airport was experiencing high winds at the time.
The aircraft landed nose wheel first, and the nose wheel collapsed after hitting a depression in the runway.
The right main landing gear leg subsequently collapsed and the aircraft left the runway.
The aircraft burst into flames and all fatalities were a result of the fire.

events.text: The pilots had to make a second landing attempt due to low visibility from haze and a harmattan.

The right main landing gear leg subsequently collapsed and the aircraft turned 180 degrees and left the runway.
The aircraft burst into flames and all fatalities were a result of the fire.

title: Libyan Arab Airlines 114
summary: Libyan Arab Airlines Flight 114, a Boeing 727, was shot down on February 21, 1973 by two Israeli F-4 fighter jets while over the Sinai Peninsula. The aircraft had become lost due to bad weather and equipment failure over northern Egypt, inadvertently entering Israeli-controlled airspace. After being intercepted by Israeli fighters, the crew was unable to receive or understand landing instructions, and the aircraft was shot down by Israeli pilot authorization.
probable_cause: The aircraft was shot down by Israeli fighter aircraft. The crew had become lost due to combination of bad weather, equipment failure, and navigation error, causing the aircraft to enter Israeli-controlled airspace where it was intercepted and shot down on authorization from Israeli military command.

title: Invicta International Airlines 435
summary: The aircraft approached Basel during a heavy snowstorm that reduced visibility significantly. Captain Anthony Dorman, who had failed his UK instrument rating test eight times and had been suspended from the Royal Canadian Air Force for lack of ability, became disoriented during the approach. He misidentified radio beacons and overflew the airport. During a second approach, Dorman based his navigation on the wrong beacon while flying at approximately 50 meters altitude. The aircraft crashed into a forested hillside near Hochwald, Switzerland.
probable_cause: The pilot became disoriented and misidentified radio beacons during the instrument approach in poor visibility. His navigation was based on wrong beacons, leading to a controlled flight into terrain at low altitude. The accident was contributed to by low visibility from heavy snowstorm and the aircraft's lack of ground proximity warning systems.

title: Aeroflot 3932
summary: Aeroflot Flight 3932 took off from Sverdlovsk-Koltsovo Airport at 18:33 MSK. During a left turn in clouds at 350 m altitude with a bank angle between 35-40 degrees, the flight crew experienced spatial disorientation due to failures in the artificial horizon and compass system caused by electrical supply failure. The bank angle reached 75-80 degrees and the crew lost complete control, crashing into forest at 270 km/h approximately five miles from Koltsovo Airport.
probable_cause: Incorrect indications by the main artificial horizon and compass system caused by failure of the electrical supply, resulting in spatial disorientation of the pilots and loss of control during a left turn in clouds.

title: Aeroflot 964
summary: The Tu-104 crashed during approach to Moscow. Navigation instruments failed and the crew lost spatial orientation. Multiple navigation instruments including the compass and artificial horizon failed. The crew lost spatial orientation in poor visibility and were unable to determine aircraft position or attitude. With correct right bank only putting the plane into a sharp left bank that reached 70 degrees, the aircraft crashed in a field 16 km northwest of Domodedovo Airport.
probable_cause: Multiple navigation instruments including the compass and artificial horizon failed. Combined with the poor visibility at the airport, the crew lost spatial orientation and were unable to see any landmarks. When the plane banked slightly to the right, the pilots corrected the right bank only to put the plane into a sharp left bank that reached 70 degrees, causing the crash.

title: Accidente de un Sud Aviation Caravelle de Royal Air Maroc en 1973
summary: The aircraft was a 12-year-old Sud Aviation Caravelle operated by Royal Air Maroc on a flight from Paris to Casablanca with a stopover in Tangier, carrying 98 passengers and 8 crew. During approach to runway 28 at Tangier-Boukhalef Airport at night in rainy weather, the aircraft made a delayed turn and entered a mountainous area. At 22:10 local time, the aircraft crashed into Mount Mellaline located 20 miles east of Tangier-Boukhalef Airport at an altitude of 2300-2400 ft, killing all 106 people on board.
probable_cause: The flight crew made a delayed turn during approach to Tangier-Boukhalef Airport at night in rainy weather, entering a mountainous area and descending below the assigned safe holding altitude of 3000 ft.
